description: The fault twin of the refusal (S65 T3, DB19): when the DISK or the FETCH fails — an unreadable root, a clone the transport refused — the answer is skills-unavailable, NOT the refusal code. The distinction is why this fixture exists: a caller that retries a refusal fixes nothing, and a caller that edits the file after a network fault is chasing the wrong thing. The what carries the failing act and the underlying sentence; nothing was written, nothing moved.

error.message: the skills catalog could not be read or fetched

data.what: skills.install acme/skills: git clone https://github.com/acme/skills.git: fatal: unable to access remote (exit status 128)
data.means: the catalog could not answer — the roots' permissions, the disk, or the network at fault; nothing was written and nothing moved
